summary:
SARlight: From Ice to Oceans is an interactive Earth-monitoring website. It explores how global warming, melting glaciers and ice sheets, and warming oceans contribute to rising sea levels and affect coastal environments around the world.
Users can explore five locations, Antarctica, Bahrain, the United Kingdom, Texas and Alaska, to learn about environmental changes, examine satellite observations and research findings, and discover possible solutions. The website also uses interactive visual features to make complex environmental information easier to understand.
This project is important because sea-level rise, coastal erosion, and land subsidence can threaten communities, infrastructure, and ecosystems. By connecting global environmental changes to local examples, especially Bahrain's vulnerable coastline, SARlight aims to raise awareness and encourage informed decisions, sustainable coastal planning and climate action.
details:
SARlight: From Ice to Oceans is an interactive website that connects satellite observations and environmental research to real-world coastal challenges. It focuses on how global warming, melting land ice and warming oceans contribute to sea-level rise, while showing how these changes affect different regions.

The website features an interactive 3D Earth with five selectable locations, Antarctica, Bahrain, the United Kingdom, Texas, and Alaska. Selecting a location opens a dedicated information page explaining the environmental issue, relevant scientific findings, its connection to global sea-level rise, and possible actions. The website also includes before and after satellite image comparisons, an overview of Antarctica's ice mass loss, and optional interactive puzzles.

The project makes scientific information more accessible by combining research, satellite imagery, interactive visuals, and practical solutions in one place. Rather than presenting climate change as a distant global issue, it connects changes in glaciers and oceans to coastal communities, ecosystems and infrastructure. Bahrain is an important case study because its low-lying coastline faces additional challenges from local land subsidence.

We used Lovable's AI-assisted website development tools to create the website and its interactive features, alongside research from NASA resources, satellite data platforms and scientific and government sources. The project was designed to make complex environmental information easier to explore and understand, while encouraging climate awareness, sustainable coastal planning, and informed action.
